title: Latency-gradient circuit breaker with shadowed fallback routing
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Problem: Our current circuit-breaker implementations are primarily threshold-based (error rate, simple latency percentiles) and trigger fallback routes that are often either too conservative (causing unnecessary model swaps) or too aggressive (causing user-visible errors). Multi-region traffic and tenant heterogeneity make fixed thresholds brittle. We need a more nuanced breaker that considers the shape of the latency distribution (the "latency gradient") and validates fallback effectiveness before switching live traffic.

Goal: Implement a Latency-Gradient Circuit Breaker (LGCB) that: (1) computes a short-window view of latency distribution shape and spike gradients (e.g., delta between P95 and P50 over time), (2) reasons across three granularities (tenant > model-dependency > global) to pick thresholds, (3) performs shadowed fallback evaluation (mirror traffic to candidate fallback) for a validation period before enabling the live fallback, and (4) safely degrades with staged shedding (prefix caching, token truncation, lower-quality model) rather than all-or-nothing switches.

Why different: The LGCB prioritizes distribution shape and trajectory (is P95 rising faster than P50?) and uses that to avoid reacting to single-point skew. Shadowed fallback provides a low-risk path to measure the real-world latency/quality tradeoffs of fallback candidates. The design must be region-aware: local circuit trips should prefer local compatible fallbacks and only escalate to cross-region/global fallback when local capacity is constrained.

Out-of-scope: full tenant billing integration for shed tokens (follow-on), and UI controls for per-tenant override (PM story separate).
acceptance_criteria: LGCB computes latency gradient metrics (P50,P75,P90,P95,P99) per 30s window and exposes them to metrics pipeline
Per-tenant, per-model, and global policies can be configured with priority ordering and explicit thresholds
Shadowed fallback mode implemented: mirrored requests to candidate fallback without affecting response path; shadow metrics logged and rolled into validation decision
Automatic activation: if shadow success rate (latency < threshold & quality checks pass) >= 95% for 5-minute validation window, live fallback may be enabled automatically (configurable)
Staged degradation strategies exist and are selectable: cache-first, prefix-serve, truncated-response, smaller-quantized-model; each stage has clear SLO and rollback criteria
Integration tests exercise per-tenant override, shadow validation, rollback after false positive, and multi-region failover scenarios
Runbook updated: playbook for manual rollback, forced-enable, and incident postmortem steps
Telemetry: dashboard with latency-gradient heatmap and shadow-vs-live comparison available in Console runtime-1.20 release
implementation_notes: Metrics: use existing runtime histograms + prom exposure; compute gradient = (P95_t - P50_t) / window_seconds and maintain EMA to smooth spikes

Config precedence: tenant config (if present) -> model dependency config -> global default. Config includes: gradient_threshold, p95_threshold_ms, sustained_window_sec, validation_window_sec, shadow_sample_rate

Shadowing: use continuous duplication at low sample rate (default 10%) for baseline; when candidate fallback considered, increase shadow_sample_rate to 100% for validation window but keep observer-only path

Validation signals: latency within threshold, error rate < 0.5%, and optional lightweight quality check (e.g., token-overlap or schema conformance for structured outputs). Validation must not return content to user or affect quotas.

Fallback types (ordered): 1) prefix/KV cache hit, 2) trimmed/early-stop generation with token budget, 3) smaller/quantized model in same region, 4) cross-region fallback to dedicated pool. Each fallback has a passthrough quality estimate and cost multiplier

Cooldown & auto-reopen: after a live fallback is enabled, require min_live_time (default 10m) and then evaluate shadowed metrics for automatic return to primary if primary recovers. Implement hysteresis: require two consecutive good windows before re-opening main path
Safety: when enabling live fallback, tag traces with fallback_reason and fallback_token_limits; ensure tracing preserves original request ID for debugging
Backpressure cooperation: interact with rate-limiter and autoscaler; when LGCB triggers shedding, signal scheduler to non-disruptively throttle low-priority tenants first
Data retention: shadowed responses stored for 7 days in encrypted bucket for offline QA; include privacy tag to drop PII per tenant settings
rollout_plan: Week 1 (canary): Deploy LGCB metrics + observer-only shadowing at 10% sample rate to runtime-stable cluster in us-west-2 (internal traffic only)
Week 2 (validation): Enable 100% shadow validation for selected non-critical tenants and one low-traffic model; collect 3 days of shadow metrics
Week 3 (staged enable): Allow auto-enable of live fallback in canary cluster for a small cohort (5% of traffic) with automatic rollback on metric regressions
Week 4 (regional expansion): Enable LGCB in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 in observer mode and verify cross-region fallbacks' latency
Week 5 (global rollout): Flip to full production with default configs; monitor SLAs and enable per-tenant opt-outs as needed
Post-rollout (2 weeks): Evaluate metrics, tune thresholds, and open follow-up tickets for UI controls and billing alignment
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert A: sustained gradient above configured threshold for more than sustained_window_sec (SEV2) -> oncall paging
Alert B: shadow validation failure rate > 5% during validation_window_sec (SEV1) -> immediate investigation
Alert C: auto-enabled live fallback success delta negative (fallback quality significantly worse than primary) -> trigger automated rollback and SEV1
Dashboard: latency-gradient heatmap per-region and per-tenant, shadow vs live latency comparison panel
SLO checks: link to runtime-1.20 SLO (p95 latency per model) and a derived SLO for fallback quality >= 95%
testing_plan: Unit tests for gradient computation and EMA smoothing
Integration test harness: synthetic traffic generator that can inject tail spikes and validate that LGCB responds as expected
Shadow validation E2E: synthetic requests with golden outputs to confirm quality checks work and mirrored responses do not leak
Chaos scenario: simulate region outage and verify cross-region fallback triggers after configured escalation time
Load test: ensure shadowing at 100% for a validation window does not overload candidate fallback (use traffic shaping in canary)
dependencies: ENG-314159 (safety-ramp-warm-handoff) - reference design for staged handoffs
k8s-scheduling - scheduler hook to signal shed tokens / priority throttling
comments: 2025-02-19 Priya Patel: Kickoff doc posted in Confluence (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/LGCB). Key design decision: gradient + shadow validation rather than pure percentile thresholds.
2025-02-22 Oliver Grant: Implemented initial gradient calculation and exposed Prom metrics (PR #2483). Observed false positives when warm caches reheat; will add EMA smoothing (next patch).
2025-02-24 SRE (Marcos Silva): Concern: 100% shadowing could double downstream load during validation. Proposed mitigation: traffic shaping + quota lease for candidate pool. Added infra dependency.
2025-02-28 Design review (Aisha Khan): Approved shadow UX for Console (shadow metrics as read-only by default). Request: add explicit tenant opt-out toggle in future PR.

2025-03-03 QA (Lina Chen): Integration test harness ready. Found an edge case where truncated-response fallback produced malformed json for some structured outputs; added lightweight schema conformance check to validation criteria.
2025-03-04 Oliver Grant: Preparing canary rollout in us-west-2. ETA for canary deploy: 2025-03-06. Next steps: run 48h observer-only and tune gradient_thresholds.
